coverage: COMPLETE FILE: all 197 stations, 0 -> 8,400 m MD (TVD to 8,364.0 m), verbatim. Full reduction constants preserved in-header: absolute gravity 980941.62 mGal (IGSN71), IGF 1967, free-air gradient -0.3085 mGal/m, reduction density 2.742 g/cm3, stated average well density 2.752 g/cm3.
data_disclosures: Surface station (0 m) carries RHO = 0.000 - the gravity reference tie, NOT a rock density; any density integral must handle it as such. GRAV is NOT strictly monotonic: repeat/tie stations (e.g. 7,162 m reading below 7,160 m) and a run-boundary discontinuity between 5,990 and 6,000 m (the tool-size change the header lists) are REAL survey structure, preserved verbatim. Station spacing is irregular (5 -> 300 m). The deep TVD divergence (MD 8,400 -> TVD 8,364.0, i.e. 36 m) is the HB's deep deviation - complementing entry 14's capture, which ends at 2,803 m where the hole is still near-perfectly vertical.
purpose: fifteenth catalogue entry - the catalogue's first REAL DENSITY PROFILE (NINTH kind): in-situ apparent density of the crust from borehole gravimetry, 2.55-2.95 g/cm3 over 8.4 km. This is the PRESSURE-side ingredient: overburden stress = integral of rho*g*dz from measured density. With entries 12 + 14, KTB-HB now carries temperature, trajectory AND density - the closed stream can describe this well's thermal state, geometry, and overburden entirely from catalogued real data.
verified: 197 stations (measured; an initial 189 estimate corrected); endpoints, surface-tie RHO=0 handling, density range, run-boundary discontinuity, and the live overburden integral (~226 MPa ~ 32,800 psi at TD) gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical file for independent re-verification
